correctness.rationale: With m=n−1 each support (i,j) uses the weight-one descendants at positions i and j−1, one output for adjacent ones and two otherwise. Any two consecutive adjacent starts collide after deleting a trailing zero from the first or leading zero from the second, when both inputs exist. Thus t+2e<=m and t<=ceil(m/2), giving the asserted upper bound. The construction uses odd singleton markers for the adjacent words and disjoint even marker pairs (4r+2,4r+4) for the nonadjacent words. After zero deletion the adjacent outputs still have gap one and disjoint start ranges {i−1,i}; the gap-three inputs yield only gaps two or three, with output first positions in disjoint ranges {4r+1,4r+2}. Unavailable boundary deletions only remove candidates. Its size ceil(m/2)+floor(m/4) equals the bound in all four residues; n=2 gives the unique input. Listing the support pairs takes O(n) word-position operations, without claiming O(n) time to print all expanded binary words. The supplied checker and its recorded finite output were inspected, not executed; the proof covers all n.
